name: Responses API — Conversation compaction
summary: Server-side and standalone context compaction for long-running Responses conversations (POST /v1/responses/compact and context_management on POST /v1/responses).
description: Responses compaction keeps long-running conversations within context limits by compacting prior turns into server-managed context. It has two surfaces: inline `context_management` on `POST /v1/responses`, which uses the generation model, and standalone `POST /v1/responses/compact`, which has its own top-level `model`.
notes:
Partial: inline `context_management` genuinely works, but the standalone `POST /v1/responses/compact` endpoint is not exposed on the Foundry project route.

**Inline `context_management` — verified end-to-end 2026-07-20 with `apim-…-openai-s/gpt-4o-mini`.** Setting `compact_threshold=1000` (server rejects `< 1000` with `integer_below_min_value`, proving the field is not silently dropped) and chaining six turns via `previous_response_id`:

| Turn | usage.total | input_items on stored response |
|-----:|------------:|---|
| 0 |  373 | `[message]` (1 item) |
| 1 |  747 | `[message, message, message]` (3) |
| 2 | 1458 | `[message, message, message, message, message]` (5) — history above threshold |
| 3 | 1492 | **`[message, compaction]`** (2) — compacted |
| 4 | 2753 | `[message, compaction]` (2) |
| 5 | 3836 | `[message, compaction]` (2) |

The stored response shows a new item of `type='compaction'` from turn 3 onward instead of the five prior turns.

**What Foundry actually sends upstream (captured in APIM for turn 3).** All prior user messages are kept verbatim, but the assistant replies are dropped and replaced by an auto-generated summary injected as an extra user message before the current turn:

> `{"role":"user", "content":"Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process. You also have access to the state of the tools that were used by that language model… ### Handoff Summary for CONTEXT CHECKPOINT COMPACTION — Two 200-word detailed paragraphs have been successfully created: Topic #0 focused on the significance of zero… Topic #1 explored the number one as a foundational concept…"}`

So compaction is performed by **Foundry's own state layer** (which explains why it works even though the upstream model only ever sees chat/completions) — it drops assistant turns, keeps user turns, and prepends a summary paragraph. This costs an extra LLM call per compact and reshapes the transcript the model sees.

**Standalone `POST /v1/responses/compact` — not exposed.** Raw REST call returns:
> `HTTP 404 DeploymentNotFound: "The API deployment for this resource does not exist…"`

See `test.py` for both probes.
